newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends lower on commercial, hedge sales.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends lower on commercial, hedge sales.

text.p: Winnipeg Commodity Exchange canola futures ended lower on hedges and commercial selling, traders said.
"Cargill sold 200 November early, then bought 500 and then we had market on close hedges," a trader said.
November WCE canola crush profit margin fell to -19.20 Monday from -18.06 Friday. Jan-Mar spread at even money, Sep-Nov $1, Nov-Jan $3. Volume was 1,400 lots, or 28,000 tonnes, with 400 hedges.
November canola futures lost $0.90 to settle at $360.90 and January ended down $0.30 at $365. Flax closed mixed, with November down $1.20 at $301 as Louis Dreyfus sold to Cargill, traders said.
Oats did not trade but commercials traded 25 December pea contracts down US$0.60 at US$167.
RBC-DS bought October western barley settled $1.30 higher at $134.40 and December was up $1.40 to $136.60 with UGG selling to commission houses, a trader said. Volume was 600 lots.
October feed wheat rose $0.70 to $158.30 as commercials sold to Cargill and LFG and Alberta Wheat Pool sold March down $0.30 at $160, a trader said. Volume was 277 lots.
(All values in Canadian dollars per tonne except oats, feed peas.)
